subject: Energy
title: Heat Pumps
description: A fast breakdown of Heat Pumps for builders.

hook.text: Heat pumps move heat instead of generating it—delivering 3–5 units of heat for every unit of electricity consumed.

buildup.text: They work like a refrigerator in reverse—extracting heat from outdoor air (even cold air) and pumping it inside.

discovery.text: A gas furnace converts fuel to heat at 95% efficiency—a heat pump achieves 300–500% by moving existing heat.

twist.text: Heat pumps also cool in summer—one device replaces both a furnace and an air conditioner, simplifying home systems.

climax.text: Europe installed 3 million heat pumps in 2022 alone—driven by the gas crisis and climate policy mandates.

punchline.text: Move heat, don't burn fuel—pumps are 3x more efficient.

quiz.question: How are heat pumps more efficient than gas furnaces?
options: They move existing heat rather than generating it
